note.subject: biology
note.title: Cell structure
note.overview: Compare eukaryotic animal and plant cells with prokaryotic bacteria. Link each structure to its function.
learningGoals: Explain the key idea using school examples.
Apply it to a short-answer or calculation question.
mustMemoriseRules: A nucleus encloses DNA in eukaryotes; bacteria have circular DNA free in the cytoplasm.
All three have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and ribosomes. Plant walls contain cellulose; bacterial walls do not.
Green leaf cells may contain chloroplasts, but onion bulb epidermal cells normally do not.
detailedExplanation: A nucleus encloses DNA in eukaryotes; bacteria have circular DNA free in the cytoplasm.
All three have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and ribosomes. Plant walls contain cellulose; bacterial walls do not.
Green leaf cells may contain chloroplasts, but onion bulb epidermal cells normally do not.
